questions.question: In the HI assay, what does inhibition of agglutination indicate?

answers.b: Presence of specific antibodies in the serum

explanations.a: RBCs are added as indicators; their absence would invalidate the test.
explanations.b: Presence of specific antibodies in the serum.
explanations.c: Complement is not involved in standard HI assays.
explanations.d: Inhibition indicates antibody neutralization, not viral genomic mutation.

questions.question: In the HI assay, what does inhibition of agglutination indicate? (Alternative)

answers.b: Presence of specific antibodies in the serum

explanations.a: Absence of RBCs would result in no red color at all, not a button.
explanations.b: Presence of specific antibodies in the serum.
explanations.c: Complement activation is not measured by HI assays.
explanations.d: Inhibition is mediated by specific antibodies binding to the viral antigen.

questions.question: A serum sample showing no agglutination at all dilutions in the HI assay indicates?

answers.a: High titre of antibodies completely inhibiting haemagglutination

explanations.a: High titre of antibodies completely inhibiting haemagglutination.
explanations.b: RBC controls verify the presence of functional cells in the assay wells.
explanations.c: High virus concentration would cause agglutination, not complete inhibition.
explanations.d: Complement lysis is not a mechanism of this agglutination inhibition test.

questions.question: What does a titre of 1:40 in an HI assay mean?

answers.a: The serum was diluted 40 times and still showed agglutination
answers.b: The serum at 1:40 dilution completely inhibited haemagglutination

explanations.a: Titre marks the highest dilution that inhibits, not causes, agglutination.
explanations.b: The serum at 1:40 dilution completely inhibited haemagglutination.
explanations.c: 4 HAU of virus are standardly used per well.
explanations.d: The percentage of agglutination is not numerically calculated in titers.

questions.question: Which of the following is a positive control in the HI assay?

answers.c: Known positive serum with antibodies against the virus
answers.d: Virus diluted beyond its HA titre

explanations.a: RBCs alone serve as the negative control (button format indicator).
explanations.b: PBS alone is a buffer control.
explanations.c: Known positive serum with antibodies against the virus.
explanations.d: Diluting virus beyond the titer acts as a check on virus strength, not positive antibody control.

questions.question: Which of the following factors can cause a false-positive inhibition in the HI assay?

explanations.a: Fresh RBCs ensure clean and accurate results.
explanations.d: Using 4 HAU is the standard requirement to prevent false results.

questions.question: What happens if more than 4 HAU of virus is used in the HI assay?

explanations.a: Excess virus will cause agglutination, masking the presence of antibodies.
explanations.b: Using too much virus decreases the sensitivity of antibody detection.
explanations.d: Virus particles clump RBCs but do not lyse them.

questions.question: What is the effect of using old or damaged red blood cells in the HI assay?

answers.b: Non-specific agglutination leading to false-positive results

explanations.a: Damaged cells decrease the reliability and sensitivity of the assay.
explanations.b: Non-specific agglutination leading to false-positive results.
explanations.c: Antibody binding is independent of RBC age, but readouts become muddy.
explanations.d: Background noise and settling stutters are increased with old cells.

questions.question: Which of the following viruses would NOT be detected by a standard HI assay?

explanations.a: Influenza viruses express haemagglutinin and are detected by HI.
explanations.b: Influenza B expresses haemagglutinin and is detected by HI.
explanations.c: Newcastle disease virus expresses HN protein and agglutinates RBCs.

questions.question: Which of the following pH ranges is optimal for PBS used in HI assays?

explanations.a: Acidic pH can cause spontaneous hemolysis or alter binding affinity.
explanations.b: Slightly acidic conditions are not optimal for cell stability.
explanations.d: Alkaline conditions can cause cell lysis or protein denaturation.
